title: Care-Home Trigger Desk: Evacuate, Shelter, Cool
one_liner: Automatic, pre-contracted action triggers that move older residents before fire, flood or heat-driven power loss becomes lethal.
customer: Multi-site senior living, assisted living and nursing operators in wildfire, coastal and heat-prone states, and their liability insurers.
problem: Older adults dominate heat, fire and hurricane deaths. Federal emergency-preparedness rules require plans but not pre-committed execution: buses, generator fuel, receiving-facility agreements and staff call-ins. Loss of power in heat kills.
solution: A facility-specific trigger sheet tied to near-real-time satellite fire detection, fire-spread modeling, AI weather ensembles and grid outage alerts. It launches staged actions: pre-contracted transport with SLAs, receiving-facility agreements, generator fuel top-ups and cooling-room setup, with an audit trail and drill simulations. Sold per bed per month.
why_now: Near-real-time satellite fire detection is getting funded and commercial (Satellites on Fire raised $2.7M), AI forecasting is cheap, and the summer 2026 heat set off demand for concrete heat plans.
revenue_model: $8-20 per bed per month, transport contract margin and insurer premium credits.
non_obvious_insight: The problem is not information but pre-committed execution. Care homes have a legal duty and insurer pressure to buy it.
first_30_days: Pilot with 3 operators in California and Colorado, build trigger sheets for 20 facilities, and sign transport partners.

title: Turnkey Recovery Amenity Operator for Landlords
one_liner: Operate managed sauna-and-cold-plunge suites inside apartment and mixed-use buildings, paid a flat monthly fee by the landlord.
customer: Owners and operators of multifamily, mixed-use and office buildings with underused fitness rooms and an amenity-arms-race problem.
problem: Insiders treat recovery as a consumer studio business (one brand went from zero to 25 contrast-therapy studios in about 20 months and plans 100 more), with retail rent, foot-traffic marketing and wet/hot-room liability. Meanwhile landlords already own the square footage and want differentiators, but cannot operate saunas and plunge tubs (cleaning, water treatment, safety, insurance).
solution: Design, install (modular saunas and tubs) and operate a recovery suite: booking app, resident access control, daily cleaning and water testing, camera-free safety monitoring, waiver and insurance management. The landlord pays a flat monthly operating fee; residents can pay small fees for guests or premium hours.
why_now: Nordic-style social wellness attendance grew about 33 percent in 2025, sauna and cold-plunge hardware is a $1B+ market and getting cheaper, and HSA-linked home sauna sales show pre-tax demand exists even without a studio.
revenue_model: $3-8k per month per property operating fee (or revenue share above a threshold) plus $40-120k build-out margin.
non_obvious_insight: The best customer for the sauna boom is not the Gen Z consumer but the landlord: acquisition cost is one sales call instead of a marketing budget, and what the landlord is really buying is zero-liability operation, not wellness.
first_30_days: Cold-outreach 100 mid-size multifamily owners in one metro with underused amenity rooms, then pilot one building with a rented modular sauna and a $3k plunge tub on a 90-day contract at about $2.5k per month while tracking resident usage and renewal intent.

title: Continuity Assurance for Emotional AI Products
one_liner: A regression-testing and escrow layer that lets companion, coaching and therapy-adjacent apps swap underlying models without users feeling the presence they know has died.
customer: Builders of AI companion, coaching, journaling and tutoring apps with 50k+ users, paying $2-10k a month, plus $15-40k per migration project.
problem: Trend chain: labs retire models every 6-12 months (OpenAI removed GPT-4o from ChatGPT on 13 Feb 2026 and the #Keep4o backlash followed), then every app on a rented model faces a forced swap, then nobody can measure whether the voice, memory use, warmth and boundaries survived. Drift toward more sycophancy is also a safety risk for vulnerable users.
solution: (1) Extract a 'persona fingerprint' (tone, boundaries, memory behavior) from historical transcripts. (2) A swap-regression suite of 300+ scenarios (comfort, boundary-setting, crisis, sycophancy, memory recall) with human-rater calibration. (3) A portable memory-and-persona bundle users can export. (4) Optional escrow of memory and configuration with a neutral custodian and a shutdown covenant.
why_now: #Keep4o proved model deprecation causes real grief. Deprecation cycles are accelerating across vendors. California SB 243 (effective Jan 2026) raises documentation duties on companion operators, and the Pew data show public distrust that punishes visible harms.
revenue_model: SaaS by monthly active users ($2-10k a month), migration projects ($15-40k), and escrow retainers (about $500 a month).
non_obvious_insight: Users do not mourn a model, they mourn a relationship state (memory plus idiolect) that the app owns and can port. The lab's model is a replaceable engine, and nobody sells the warmth-preserving transmission between engines.
first_30_days: Interview 15 companion and coaching founders. Build a v0 eval on three open-weight model pairs. Offer free 'swap audits' to three apps, then convert the two most nervous ones to paid.

title: Blind Spend Tokens for Secretive Buyer Agents
one_liner: A buyer-side privacy gateway that lets agents pay for data and APIs with unlinkable tokens that prove 'authorized and funded' without revealing who is asking, what the price ceiling is, or what the question was.
customer: Buy-side and R&D organizations whose queries are the secret: hedge funds and asset managers, pharma competitive-intelligence and BD teams, M&A law firms and defense contractors that route agents to paid data, patent, expert-network and search APIs.
problem: Agent commerce protocols hand the seller the buyer's leverage by design. Signed mandates state a maximum price and intent, agent IDs let vendors profile and price-discriminate, and the queries themselves (a ticker, a compound, a patent family) reveal research direction. Query logs can leak, be resold or be front-run.
solution: A gateway sitting between the buyer's agents and vendors. Blind-signed, unlinkable spend tokens (Privacy Pass style) are issued after KYC by a bank or escrow, so the vendor is guaranteed payment but cannot identify the buyer. Mandates are committed and proven within cap using a zero-knowledge range proof or a TEE mediator, so the ceiling is never disclosed. Queries are batched, cached and mixed with decoys across a pooled anonymity set of customers.
why_now: Signed-agent identity and KYA schemes are proliferating across card networks and web standards, all oriented toward reassuring sellers. Privacy Pass is now a set of IETF standards. Agents issue thousands of paid queries per day, so leakage volume has exploded.
revenue_model: $8-25k per month per firm plus 0.5-1% of pass-through spend. A one-time $15k query-leakage audit is the entry product.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone is building 'know your agent' for the seller's benefit. The buyer's reservation price and research intent are the real assets, and privacy for the buyer is unclaimed territory. For funds, leaked query patterns are alpha decay, which gives a hard-dollar budget line. The chicken-and-egg problem of anonymity sets is solved by starting with decoy traffic and TEE-operated pooling.
first_30_days: Sell 5 query-leakage audits ($15k each) to funds and pharma CI teams: instrument what their agents leak to vendors (headers, mandates, IPs, query text) and deliver a report. Turn the audit findings into a decoy-plus-proxy gateway for the three data vendors most used by early customers.

title: Pay Home Inspectors to Find Lead Pipes
one_liner: A micro-bounty network that pays home inspectors, plumbers and water-heater installers to photograph where the service line enters the basement, with AI classification, so utilities can clear 'unknown material' lines for about $40 each instead of $500-3,000 each.
customer: Mid-size municipal and district water utilities (20k-300k connections) with a large 'unknown material' share in their published lead service line inventory. The buyer is the utility director or the lead program manager. A secondary payer is the home buyer, who pays about $29 for a 'Lead Line Certificate' add-on at inspection.
problem: Since the lead and copper inventory requirement, every system has had to classify each service line as lead, galvanized-requiring-replacement, non-lead or unknown. Unknowns are a legal and financial liability, and they are hard to shrink. The only sure verification is potholing or excavation, which costs hundreds to thousands of dollars per line. Customer self-ID by mailer gets a response rate of roughly 10-25%. Absentee landlords and LLCs almost never answer. Utility crews can't look inside private basements, so tens of thousands of unknowns sit in the spreadsheet for years.
solution: A mobile app with a fixed 3-photo protocol: the pipe where it enters the building, a scratch or magnet test close-up, and the meter serial number with the address. A vision model classifies the pipe as copper, galvanized, lead, PEX, PVC or HDPE, or flags it as unresolved. Humans QA the low-confidence cases. Each submission is geo-verified and tamper-evident, and exports in the format the state inventory portal expects. Inspectors and plumbers earn $15-25 per verified line, and the platform earns the spread. The utility gets a reconciled inventory feed and a dashboard showing unknowns falling by ZIP code. The consumer add-on (inspector-branded certificate, sold to the buyer) pays the inspector while giving the utility free data.
why_now: The first inventories were filed in late 2024, and public analyses showed millions of lines still classified 'unknown'. The Lead and Copper Rule Improvements set a 10-year replacement clock that starts around 2027, though federal details keep being revisited and litigated. Several states have their own replacement statutes that don't depend on the federal rule. The $15B in dedicated infrastructure-law lead line money is moving through state revolving funds under spend-down pressure. Vision models are only now accurate enough to classify pipe photos. (Regulatory details are from memory. Verify state acceptance rules before pitching.)
revenue_model: Utilities pay $30-60 per verified line, sold as a per-line contract that fits under small-purchase thresholds. A $10-25k pilot is typical, followed by annual contracts. The consumer-paid certificate ($29) is split with the inspector. Later products are inventory-reconciliation SaaS and an access-agreement workflow for replacement crews.
non_obvious_insight: Utilities think they have a data problem, but they have an eyeballs-in-basements problem. Every home sale (an inspector visits) and every water heater swap (a plumber stands three feet from the service entry) already puts a paid expert next to the exact pipe that matters. Nobody has paid them for a photo yet. Excavation is the wrong tool for a question that visual inspection answers for almost nothing.
first_30_days: Pick one state that accepts documented visual or contractor verification. Pick two utilities in it whose public inventories are more than 40% unknown. Recruit 30 inspectors through local InterNACHI and ASHI chapter meetups and Facebook groups, and pay a launch bonus per photo set. Run a 200-line pilot. Have the utility pothole 30 of those lines as ground truth, then publish the accuracy numbers. Close a $15-25k pilot purchase order with the first utility, using the small-purchase limit that many cities set at $25-50k so no council vote is needed.

title: Rebuild-Cost Audit Sold Through Agents' E&O Fear
one_liner: A 15-minute independent rebuild-cost check at renewal that documents limits, sold to the agents and E&O carriers who hold the underinsurance tail.
customer: Independent agencies in California, Colorado and Florida and their E&O program managers. Wealth advisors and trust attorneys for high-value homes are a second channel.
problem: In the Palisades, insurer estimates run about $462/sq ft against contractor budgets up to $1,065, and only about 13% of owners have started rebuilding. Part of that gap is contractor premium, but a large part is stale valuation. Owners are underinsured, and the agents who sold the limits carry E&O exposure. Renewals in 2026-27 are the moment to fix it.
solution: A rebuild reality check that pulls permit records, local bid data, post-disaster cost surge and home features. It outputs a defensible range and recommended limits or extended replacement cost, with contractor validation for the top decile of homes. It is white-labeled by the agent, and the audit log doubles as an E&O defense file.
why_now: The LA fire claims experience is now public and quantified, so E&O carriers and agencies finally have a concrete loss to point at.
revenue_model: $29-99 per policy to the agency, or a program fee from an E&O carrier that gives premium credits. A $299 tier adds a contractor walk-through.
non_obvious_insight: The economic buyer is not the homeowner but the agent's E&O carrier, who wants documentation. Underinsurance is the biggest unpriced tail left after the LA fires.
first_30_days: Calibrate on 100 posted Palisades and Altadena claim outcomes. Pitch 5 agencies with high-value books, and approach one agency E&O program manager about a documented-audit premium credit.

title: Supplier-side questionnaire firewall citing the VSME cap
one_liner: A forward-to tool that answers big customers' ESG, NIS2 and EUDR questionnaires from one evidence vault and flags which questions the law says a small supplier can decline.
customer: EU SMEs and small mid-caps (under 1,000 staff) that supply larger companies, bought through accountants, tax advisors and chambers of commerce who add it as a service to their clients.
problem: Since Omnibus I took effect on 18 March 2026, CSRD-scope buyers cannot require value-chain partners with 1,000 or fewer employees to provide more sustainability information than the voluntary SME standard (VSME) sets out. The VSME basic module covers business description, workforce, energy and Scope 1 and 2 emissions. The cap does not cover NIS2 security questionnaires, EUDR data, voluntary customer targets or bid competition. Suppliers still get differently formatted questionnaires from every customer and lender, and most cannot tell which asks are legally capped.
solution: Suppliers forward each customer questionnaire (Excel, PDF or portal export) to an inbox. The tool parses it and maps each question to a canonical evidence vault: VSME basic answers, energy and payroll-derived Scope 1 and 2 numbers, a NIS2-lite control evidence set, and a supplier code of conduct. It auto-drafts answers. It also classifies every question as 'inside the cap', 'outside the cap, with a cited polite decline paragraph', or 'not covered by the cap (NIS2, EUDR, voluntary)'. The vault is built by pulling data the accountant already holds. Accountants get a multi-client dashboard.
why_now: The cap is 6 months old and the VSME Delegated Act was published in July 2026, so customers' procurement teams are still sending old-format questionnaires. Germany's NIS2 law took effect on 6 Dec 2025 and BSI says regulated entities will grow from about 4,500 to about 29,500, which multiplies supplier security questionnaires. CSDDD also limits information requests to smaller firms, but application is not until 2029.
revenue_model: White-label to accountancies at EUR 15-30 per client per month, or direct at EUR 49-99 per month per SME. Add EUR 150-300 for a one-off 'initial vault build' for firms not served by an accountant.
non_obvious_insight: The crowded market sells to large buyers who send questionnaires. The legally new wedge is the supplier's right to refuse, plus the accountant, who already holds energy and payroll data and is trusted. Evidence: after 18 March 2026 large CSRD companies 'cannot require value-chain partners with 1,000 or fewer employees to provide more sustainability information than ... VSME', but the same source warns that 'Nothing stops a buyer choosing the bidder who turned up with clean, current numbers' and that Scope 1 and 2 are non-negotiable, so suppliers need both a decline lever and a ready pack (https://www.dashe.ai/blog/big-customer-asked-for-your-emissions/). Suppliers to NIS2 entities 'should expect questionnaires' and sending a 300-question form is common (https://www.3rdrisk.com/blog/seven-nis2-questions-to-ask). Germany's NIS2 registration had only 38.5% compliance by the March 2026 deadline (https://www.cloudmagazin.com/en/2026/03/22/nis2-and-saas-supply-chain-compliance-gap/).
first_30_days: Collect 30 real questionnaires by offering accountants a free 'questionnaire triage' in exchange for the redacted files. Hand-map them to a 60-row canonical answer sheet. Build the classify-and-decline prototype on that set. Pitch 5 small accounting firms and 2 chamber-of-commerce sustainability desks with a live demo on a client's own questionnaire. Aim for 3 paying accountancy pilots.

title: Live-In Guardians for Probate Houses
one_liner: Vetted live-in 'guardians' keep a house occupied while an estate is in probate, so the executor keeps insurance validity, avoids vacancy losses and pays less than for a vacant-home policy.
customer: Executors, estate and probate attorneys, professional fiduciaries and out-of-state heirs holding an inherited house. Attorneys are the channel, and executors and estates pay.
problem: Probate sales often take 6 to 12 months or longer. Most homeowners policies limit or exclude coverage after 30 to 60 days of vacancy, so a burst pipe, vandal or squatter can leave the estate uncovered, and specialty vacant-home policies cost far more. The executor is a non-expert with fiduciary liability, often living out of state, and has no one to check the house.
solution: Place screened guardians (night-shift nurses, travel clinicians, grad students, apprentice tradespeople) in probate houses under a state-specific license agreement rather than a lease. Guardians pay a low monthly fee, keep utilities on, handle mail and lawn, and file daily check-in logs. The estate gets an 'occupied' attestation accepted by a partner insurer or MGA, monthly photo reports, and a house that shows better at sale time. Upsell cleanout and staging at sale.
why_now: Boomer estates are moving through probate in growing numbers, and homeowners insurers are tightening on nonrenewals and vacancy. Housing costs are high enough that many good tenants will accept a small duty load for below-market housing. UK-style property guardianship exists for commercial buildings, but the US probate house niche is open.
revenue_model: Estate pays $250 to $500 per month service fee. Guardian pays a program fee. Carrier or MGA commission on the policy. Fees on cleanout, staging and sale-transition services.
non_obvious_insight: The customer isn't buying a house sitter; the estate is buying continued insurance validity and a checklist that satisfies a fiduciary. Occupied status changes the risk class of the asset for the whole probate period. Legal structure (license, not lease, chosen state by state) is the real product and the barrier to copycats.
first_30_days: Pitch 15 probate and estate-planning attorneys in one metro on a pilot for their next three vacant homes. Recruit guardians through hospital and travel-nurse groups. Have a landlord-tenant attorney draft the license and pick a landlord-friendly state to start (for example Texas or Tennessee). Line up a vacant-dwelling insurance broker who will recognize the guardian arrangement. First revenue within about six weeks.

title: Immunogenicity Screens for De Novo Proteins
one_liner: A fast, low-cost HLA-diverse T-cell screen and de-immunize-and-retest loop built for AI-designed proteins that have no natural template to humanize.
customer: AI protein-design startups and pharma teams with de novo miniprotein or binder programs approaching IND, and design-tool vendors who want immunogenicity data as proof of quality.
problem: Trend chain: AI binder design is cheap and abundant. Designs are entering the clinic (a de novo PD-L1 miniprotein has reached first-in-human imaging). But de novo proteins have no germline or humanization playbook, in silico epitope predictors over-call risk, and ex vivo T-cell panels are custom studies at CROs. PBMC vials cost about $460 each, so early-stage designers skip the test until a late failure.
solution: Bulk-buy an HLA-typed donor PBMC bank (30-50 donors covering major alleles). Run 96-well T-cell activation and proliferation assays plus MHC-associated peptide analysis on batches of 20-100 candidates per week. Return per-sequence hotspot maps, feed AI deimmunization redesign, then retest. Publish calibration against known immunogenic and non-immunogenic clinical proteins.
why_now: AI-drug funding tops $6B in 2026, and frontier-lab designs hit about 27% in Adaptyv's blind test, so many de novo programs are heading toward IND. FDA's shift toward human-relevant in vitro methods favors ex vivo immunogenicity assays.
revenue_model: $2-5k per candidate at batch scale, $50-150k for full deimmunization campaigns, and platform subscriptions for design companies.
non_obvious_insight: The cost driver is donors, not reagents. Buying donor lots at scale and running big plate batches flips the economics from 'per-molecule custom study' to 'per plate'. Every screen also calibrates the predictors that AI designers will later pay for, which builds a data flywheel.
first_30_days: Contract an existing immunology lab staffed by ex-CRO scientists. Order 30 HLA-typed PBMC lots at bulk pricing. Test 10 published de novo binders and 5 clinical reference proteins. Publish a preprint and pitch 10 protein-design startups.

title: Robot Finger That Makes Legacy Instruments Agent-Operable
one_liner: A camera-plus-servo retrofit box that presses buttons, turns knobs and reads displays on validated lab and test equipment from the outside, giving decade-old instruments an API without touching their software.
customer: QC and analytical labs in pharma and CDMOs, food and environmental testing labs, university core facilities, and small biotechs running out-of-support equipment such as plate readers, autoclaves, centrifuges, HPLC pumps, stability chambers and test benches.
problem: Lab automation assumes new, API-enabled instruments, but the installed base is 10-20-year-old boxes with front panels only. In GxP and ISO 17025 labs, changing instrument firmware or software can trigger revalidation, which blocks IT-style integration. Scientists and agents still want unattended overnight runs, scheduling and structured logs.
solution: A clamp-on or adhesive module with 2-6 servos for buttons, knobs and a touchscreen stylus, a wide-angle camera, and a vision-language model that reads 7-segment displays, LCDs and status LEDs. A confirm-after-every-action loop and hard interlocks make it safe. It exposes an MCP and REST endpoint ('start program 4', 'read temperature', 'log state') and keeps video plus state log as the audit trail. It sits outside the validated boundary as 'operator-equivalent', so only the actuator needs qualification.
why_now: Vision-language models now read messy panels cheaply and reliably, and servo and edge-compute costs are trivial. Autonomous-lab offerings such as Ginkgo Cloud Lab prove scientists want agent-run experiments, but they require shipping samples to a vendor's lab. Most labs still own and must keep using their own equipment.
revenue_model: $400-900 hardware per instrument, $40-100 per month per device for scheduling, audit trail and the agent endpoint, and $2-5k per site for IQ/OQ qualification templates.
non_obvious_insight: Revalidation cost, not technology, blocks lab automation. An actuator that does exactly what a technician's finger does sidesteps change control, so selling 'validation-friendly' beats selling 'smart'. The video-verified state log is also a better audit trail than most instruments produce natively.
first_30_days: Build 3 prototypes from off-the-shelf servos, cameras and a Raspberry Pi-class board. Interview 20 QC lab managers and core-facility directors. Offer free two-week pilots on one autoclave or plate reader that runs a nightly routine, then convert to a $3k paid pilot including an IQ/OQ document.

title: Robot Pilot Guild for Gaming-Native Gen Z
one_liner: A guild that recruits, trains and certifies gamers aged 16-25 to remotely pilot delivery robots and humanoids, with a portable verified flight-hour logbook that becomes their credential.
customer: Robotics and physical-AI companies (sidewalk delivery, warehouse, humanoid pilots) that buy validated pilot-hours and demonstration data. Workforce boards and trainees pay for certification.
problem: Robots in 2026 run on human backup: remote assistance for stuck delivery robots and teleoperated demonstrations to train humanoids. Companies staff this ad hoc through BPOs and labeling vendors, with high churn, uneven quality and no career ladder. US lab teleoperator roles are already posting at $30-$55 per hour. Gen Alpha and Gen Z raised on controllers have the reflexes but no legitimate on-ramp.
solution: Regional 'pilot houses' with standardized rigs plus at-home certification. A tiered license runs from Level 1 sidewalk assist to Level 3 dexterous manipulation, tested in simulation and on real robots. The guild is the W-2 employer of record, sells SLA-bound pilot capacity by the validated hour, and records verified hours in a portable logbook like aviation. Quality is managed through replay review and per-task acceptance rates.
why_now: Teleoperation sits at the center of humanoid and home-robot programs in 2026 (home humanoids such as 1X NEO ship with remote operators), and demonstration data is being bought like compute. Entry-level white-collar hiring is weak, so young people want alternative on-ramps. Robot companies need reliable operator supply now, not in 2030.
revenue_model: $25-$45 per validated pilot-hour billed to robot companies, targeting about 40% gross margin. Certification fees of $200-$600 paid by trainees, workforce funds or employers, plus placement fees when companies hire pilots directly.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset in physical AI is consistent, high-quality human motor demonstration, and Gen Alpha has been practicing exactly that skill for a decade. A verified flight-hour logbook turns play into a portable credential. That makes workers stickier and quality auditable, so this is a licensed guild employer rather than a gig marketplace.
first_30_days: Approach three sidewalk-delivery or warehouse-robot startups with visible remote-assist queues. Offer a paid 4-week pilot with 10 trained gamers recruited from Discord communities and community-college esports programs. Train them on the customer's own simulator and bill per validated hour. Goal: one signed pilot and one letter of intent for a 50-pilot cohort.

title: The Second Ceremony After Direct Cremation
one_liner: A scattering-day and celebration-of-life concierge for the majority of families who chose cremation with no service and later realize they need a ritual.
customer: Adult children aged 40 to 65, two to twelve months after a direct cremation of a parent. Channels: online direct-cremation providers, hospice social workers and estate attorneys.
problem: The NFDA projects a 63.4% US cremation rate for 2025, rising toward 82% by 2045, and direct cremation ($1,000 to $3,000, no viewing, no service) is the fastest-growing segment. Families later improvise: an urn in a closet, a scattering with unclear legality, a restaurant back room. Funeral homes make nothing on this, and direct-cremation providers do not offer events.
solution: Fixed-price packages. Scattering day: jurisdiction-specific permit and rule guidance, boat or site scouting, a celebrant, a biodegradable urn, photographer or drone, and a livestream for distant relatives. Celebration of life: venue, catering, an AI-assisted slideshow built from the family's photos, an officiant, a guestbook and thank-you notes. Keepsake add-ons such as glass, vinyl, reef or tree. A planner keyed to 'days since death' nudges families at 30, 60 and 90 days.
why_now: Direct cremation took off with online price comparison, and the NFDA's 2025 report finds most people (58.3%) have attended a funeral at a non-traditional location. AI makes the slideshow, program and eulogy drafting cheap. Cremation providers are looking for post-sale revenue and a 'what now' answer for customers.
revenue_model: $900 to $4,500 per event: a $500 to $1,200 coordination fee plus 15% to 25% margin on boats, venues and catering. A 10% to 15% referral share to cremation providers that embed the offer. Annual remembrance add-on.
non_obvious_insight: Direct cremation removed the ceremony from the funeral bundle, and the vacuum reappears months later when the buyer is calmer, has a longer planning horizon and pays for meaning rather than logistics. The unbundled piece is the second funeral, and it can be more profitable than the first because there is no legacy funeral-home cost base.
first_30_days: Choose a coastal city such as San Diego, Seattle or Boston. Contract two licensed boat charters, three celebrants and a photographer. Write one-page scattering compliance sheets for the local jurisdictions. Interview hospice social workers to find referrals, and offer 10 founding families a $650 scattering-day package. Ask two direct-cremation providers to link the offer from their post-cremation emails, and aim for five events by month three.

title: Mother-Tongue Lifeline for Dementia Flashpoints
one_liner: On-demand live video calls where a dementia-trained speaker of the patient's first language and dialect coaches the English-speaking aide and calms the patient at bath, bedtime and exit-seeking moments.
customer: Home care agencies and PACE programs in immigrant-dense metros (NYC, LA, Miami, Chicago, Bay Area, Houston) with dementia clients whose aides do not share their language. Second: Medicaid managed long-term care and D-SNP plans. Third: families on a flat monthly plan.
problem: Bilingual and multilingual patients lose their second language as dementia advances and drift back to the language, dialect and idioms of their childhood. Agencies send whoever is available. The English-speaking aide cannot say the one calming phrase during the bath, so the bath fails, the patient panics, the aide gets hurt or quits, and the family blames the agency. Telephone interpretation lines translate literally, but a dementia patient's fragments and proverbs need to be validated, not translated. It is a communication problem, not an interpretation problem.
solution: A dedicated line, staffed on demand by trained bilingual retirees, nurses and teachers, covering the long tail: Yiddish, Haitian Creole, Toisanese, Cantonese, Polish, Russian, Uzbek, Punjabi, Tagalog, Greek, Armenian. A tablet or phone is propped where the patient can see it. The specialist speaks to the patient in dialect while coaching the aide in English in the earpiece: 'she's asking for her sister, say she is coming, then hum this song.' Sessions are 3-10 minutes at known flashpoints. Specialists are trained by aides in validation and redirection, not interpretation.
why_now: The post-war Soviet, Chinese, Caribbean and Southeast Asian immigrant cohorts who arrived in the 1960s-80s are now reaching moderate-to-severe dementia. Low-latency video is universal and cheap. AI companions such as KindredMind (voice clone of the caregiver, 12 languages, launched worldwide in May 2026) prove the demand, but they work best for mild cases and comfortable tech users. For moderate-to-severe dementia and live crises, the warm human voice in the right village dialect is the missing complement, and the agencies will pay per minute for it.
revenue_model: $1.25-1.75 per minute billed to agencies and plans, with 60-70 percent gross margin after specialist pay of about $0.45 per minute. Families get $129 per month for 20 sessions. Later, enterprise contracts with MLTC and D-SNP plans that cover the cost as a quality tool.
non_obvious_insight: Patients revert not just to a language but to a specific dialect and era, for example Toisanese, not Mandarin, and the idioms of 1955. A literal interpreter is useless because what calms is tone, a lullaby, a proverb and a familiar name. The buyer is not the family but the agency, which is desperate because language mismatch is why its aides quit its hardest cases. Nobody pays interpreters for companionship, so this talent pool of bilingual retirees is unmined and cheap.
first_30_days: Pick two languages with dense local demand, for example Toisanese or Cantonese in NYC and Haitian Creole in Miami. Recruit 10 bilingual retirees through churches, senior centers and community media. Train them in a one-page validation script. Run it on WhatsApp video with no software. Call 15 small agencies serving those communities and offer 30 free minutes per case. Sign the first three at $1.50 per minute with a $300 monthly minimum.

title: Satiety Peptides for Small-Portion Foods
one_liner: Screen food-grade peptides that trigger the body's own GLP-1 release and put them in high-protein snacks.
customer: Protein bar, yogurt and snack brands serving GLP-1 users and people coming off the drugs.
problem: Small-portion products leave consumers unsatisfied, and CPG incumbents lack anything that helps portions feel sufficient.
solution: ML-screened protein hydrolysate peptides verified in enteroendocrine cell assays for GLP-1 secretion, supplied as an ingredient with structure-function claims only.
why_now: About 12% of Americans use GLP-1s, snack volume is shifting, and AI peptide prediction plus cheap CRO assays let a small team screen quickly.
revenue_model: Ingredient supply and licensing with per-kg pricing and development fees.
non_obvious_insight: GLP-1 drugs created a mass vocabulary for satiety, so food can compete at the margins of lower-dose and post-drug users without making any drug claim.
first_30_days: Hydrolyze two cheap protein streams, run an in vitro GLP-1 secretion assay through a CRO, and sample results to five snack brands.

title: Fake-Support Scam Takedown for Fintechs
one_liner: A monitoring and takedown service that finds scammers posing as your customer support in public help threads, clusters them by phone, WhatsApp and Telegram identifiers, and kills them fast with regulator-ready evidence files.
customer: Fraud, trust & safety and CX heads at crypto exchanges, wallet makers, neobanks, BNPL and payment providers. Start with mid-market crypto/fintech ($5M-$50M ARR), then EU payment service providers. Roughly $3k-$10k per month.
problem: Every 'my account is locked' thread in a fintech or crypto subreddit gets a friendly stranger reply within minutes, then a DM pushing a WhatsApp or Telegram 'support agent'. Mods remove the comments, but the brand never sees removed comments or DMs. The same 20-50 phone numbers and handles recycle week after week, and victims are usually novices or seniors. Mods keep private spreadsheets of these identifiers, and nobody aggregates them for the brand being impersonated.
solution: Monitor public help venues (Reddit through licensed access or partners, plus X, Facebook groups, YouTube comments, Google Business listings, review-site replies and search ads) for support-impersonation patterns. Extract the contact identifiers, graph-cluster them into campaigns, and file takedowns with WhatsApp/Telegram, telcos, registrars and platforms. Produce timestamped evidence packs for refund disputes and regulators. Give each brand a pre-registered 'official support channels' beacon that community mods can add to a sticky or AutoMod reply for free, cutting victim conversion without any content moderation. Mods are never paid, and the data flows to them.
why_now: The EU PSR/PSD3 political agreement of 27 November 2025 makes payment providers refund customers in bank-employee impersonation scams and makes online platforms liable to those providers if they fail to remove notified fraudulent content. Notification evidence and takedown speed now have a dollar value. The UK's mandatory APP-fraud reimbursement (since October 2024) already priced this risk. LLM-written scam scripts are fluent, which defeats keyword filters.
revenue_model: SaaS subscription of $3k-$10k per month per brand, a per-takedown premium tier, evidence-pack retainers for payment providers in the EU, and later an identifier feed sold to telcos and platforms.
non_obvious_insight: The scam's weak point is the contact channel, not the message. Fluent AI text is cheap, but the phone numbers, handles and domains are a small recyclable set, so identifier graphs beat content classifiers. Mod removal logs also hold the ground truth on how many minutes a scam reply survives, which brands can't see and which now matters for liability. An 'official channels' sticky is the cheapest conversion-killer there is.
first_30_days: Build a free 'exposure audit' for 10 mid-size crypto and fintech brands: a 30-day scan of public threads, X and Google Business listings that shows them 40 live scam identifiers and how long each survived. Send each fraud lead their own brand's data. Convert 2 into $2.5k/month paid pilots. Partner with 3 volunteer mod teams of fintech subreddits, giving them free tooling and taking labeled ground truth in return, with no payment to mods.

title: H.264 Royalty Sunset Desk for Streamers
one_liner: A country-by-country patent-expiry analysis and codec-delivery plan that cuts H.264/AVC streaming royalty exposure for mid-tier video services, paid partly on savings.
customer: Mid-size OTT and FAST channel operators, ed-tech, fitness, telehealth and cloud-gaming platforms and video-heavy social apps (well below the 100M-subscriber mega-tier). Buyer is the general counsel, CFO or head of video engineering.
problem: The Via LA AVC pool replaced its flat $100k streaming cap with tiered fees up to $4.5M a year, and added FAST and cloud-gaming categories, for a codec standardized in 2003. Press reports say US patent coverage runs out around 2028, so one analysis says paying $4.5M for about 18 months of coverage 'makes no economic sense'. Wikipedia and HN commenters put at least one US patent at 2030 and 'only 5 left' worldwide. Mid-tier operators can't tell what they actually owe.
solution: Ingest Via LA's public AVC patent attachment (re-issued 2026-09-28) plus national legal-status data, and build a live-patent map per country. Overlay each customer's audience by country and device. Deliver (a) a counsel-ready exposure memo to negotiate the right tier or challenge scope, (b) an engineering plan that serves AV1/VP9 in territories with live patents and H.264 where none remain, using a device-capability ladder, and (c) a countdown dashboard that also tracks HEVC and audio codecs. Work with a patent attorney partner so the memo is legal work product.
why_now: The new streaming fee schedule took effect in early 2026 (Tom's Hardware, Apr 3, 2026: fees raised 'from $100,000 up to $4.5 million'). The last MPEG-4 Part 2 patent expired 2026-07-19 and the last E-AC3 patents may have lapsed in 2026, so 'is it free yet?' is a live question. AV1 hardware decode is now common in 2023+ phones, TVs and PCs.
revenue_model: Fixed $15k-$40k audit and plan, plus about 20% of first-year royalty savings or avoided fees, plus $1k a month for the monitoring dashboard.
non_obvious_insight: Patent pools price by audience tier, not by how many patents are still alive, and patents are territorial and expire on different dates, so the expiry calendar itself is arbitrage. Evidence: Via LA's program page shows Tier 1 at $4.5M a year, small operators as low as $100k, new FAST and cloud-gaming tiers, and a patent attachment updated 2026-09-28 (https://www.via-la.com/licensing-2/avc-h-264/). The Wikipedia AVC entry notes many patents expired but at least one US patent runs to Nov 2030, and that Nokia sued HP and Amazon over H.264/H.265 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advanced_Video_Coding). The HN thread on the last Brazilian MPEG-4 patent expiring includes 'only 5 left' and a Siemens patent to 2030 (https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/items/49311814). Details of the expired Siemens BR patent: https://www.xda-developers.com/25-year-old-brazilian-video-patent-expired-legal-headache-linux/.
first_30_days: Days 1-14: scrape the Via LA patent list and build the per-country expiry table for AVC (a few weekends of work). Days 10-30: post the free 'H.264 patent death clock' as a public page, pitch 30 mid-size streaming and video-first SaaS companies from job boards and app-store data with a free exposure estimate, and offer a $7.5k pilot audit to the first 3 who reply. Retain a patent attorney on a flat fee to sign off on memo templates.

title: Warm-Backup Servicer for Orphaned Solar
one_liner: Be the standby operations-and-maintenance contractor for lenders and securitization trustees holding portfolios of systems whose installer died.
customer: Trustees and servicers of solar loan and lease securitizations, tax-equity and debt holders, and buyers of distressed portfolios. Homeowners can buy direct as a secondary channel.
problem: Sunnova, Titan, ADT Solar and Freedom Forever failed. Manufacturer warranties survive but nobody supplies the service labor, and monitoring clouds die. Customers with dead inverters stop paying, which erodes the cash flows lenders depend on.
solution: A backup-servicing contract. Onboard the portfolio's asset data, replace dead monitoring clouds with a local gateway, dispatch vetted local technicians through a roll-up network, handle manufacturer RMA and warranty claims, and upsell battery retrofit and VPP enrollment.
why_now: The bankruptcy wave of 2024-26 has portfolios sitting in trustees' hands. With 25D gone there are fewer new installers. A 46% storage attach rate means more complex systems in the field.
revenue_model: $8-15 per system-month standby retainer, a $250-450 margin per truck roll, an RMA handling fee, and referral fees for battery and VPP enrollments.
non_obvious_insight: Lenders do not care about kilowatts. They care about payments, and a homeowner with a dead inverter stops paying. Service is a credit-protection product, and its buyer is the party with the balance sheet and the pain.
first_30_days: Identify three distressed portfolios from trustee reports and call the servicers. Sign a 1,000-system pilot in one metro. Onboard two local service shops. Build the gateway on vendor APIs and local Modbus.

title: Age-Signal Rules Engine for App Developers
one_liner: A 'feature-flag service for minors' law': an SDK that takes the OS or app-store age bracket plus jurisdiction and returns the legally required feature set, with citations and an audit trail.
customer: Mid-size consumer apps, games and edtech (10-500 staff) with under-18 users, their general counsel, and app agencies. Series A-C startups first.
problem: Texas app-store age verification (June 2026), Ohio consent (June 2026), Florida under-14 ban, California's OS age-attestation law, the UK regime, and bans in Australia, Brazil, Indonesia and Malaysia each define brackets and required behavior differently. Engineers hard-code rules and rules change monthly. Fines are large.
solution: A versioned policy graph maintained by lawyers plus LLM change tracking. The SDK returns flags for chat, DMs, push timing, ads, purchases and recommendation feeds per bracket and jurisdiction. It integrates with OS age-range signals and third-party verifiers and logs which rule applied when, for regulators.
why_now: For the first time OS and app stores hand developers an age signal (California signed Oct 2025; Apple and Google age-range APIs, from memory), but nobody says what to do with it. The 'policy ratchet' means fragmentation will grow.
revenue_model: $500-5k a month by MAU tier, plus one-time compliance-matrix audits at $3-6k.
non_obvious_insight: Age-verification vendors sell the signal, and nobody sells the decision: the legal mapping from signal to product behavior. That mapping is the durable moat because laws keep diverging.
first_30_days: Publish a public 8-jurisdiction by 5-feature matrix. Run a newsletter around it. Sell 5 compliance-matrix audits at $4k to game and app teams. Wrap the logic into an SDK by month 3.

title: Deposit Gate That Kills Korean Bulk-Order Scams
one_liner: A KakaoTalk-native verify-and-deposit link that small Korean restaurants, bakeries and caterers send to any big or suspicious order, since scammers never pay a deposit and real customers do.
customer: Korean self-employed food, bakery, flower and catering owners who take phone or chat bulk orders. They pay ₩9,900/month plus a 1.5-2.5% take rate on deposits. Restaurant and bakery associations, POS vendors and card acquirers are distribution partners.
problem: The 'no-show scam' impersonates a government office, military unit, broadcaster or political party and places a large legitimate-looking order. The scammer then asks the owner to buy unrelated goods from a designated supplier, promising to pay for everything together. The owner pays the fake supplier and loses the money. It is 100% preventable by process, yet owners are alone on the phone and busy.
solution: The owner taps a Kakao chatbot or shortcut during the call. The caller receives a verify-and-deposit link: PASS phone identity, a claimed-organization check against official directories with call-back numbers, and a 10-30% deposit via KakaoPay or Toss. A tripwire flags any request to buy from a third-party supplier, which is the hallmark of stage two of the scheme. Scams die at the deposit step. Legitimate bulk buyers pay a small deposit, which also cuts ordinary no-shows.
why_now: H1 2025 losses were roughly 90% of the whole of 2024, with per-case damage up more than 50% year on year. Scammers keep widening the impersonations to entertainment agencies, broadcasters and political parties. Authorities' advice is already 'ask for a deposit', but nothing operationalizes it for a shop owner. KakaoPay and Toss make micro-deposit links trivial.
revenue_model: ₩9,900/month per shop, plus 1.5-2.5% of each deposit processed. B2B2C licensing to POS and reservation vendors, and fraud-loss underwriting data for card and insurance partners.
non_obvious_insight: The theft is not the food order, it is the redirected procurement in stage two, so a single rule ('never buy from a supplier the customer names') is nearly precision-perfect and a deposit is a perfect filter. Police-reported H1 2025 damage was ₩115.5 billion (1,155억 won) across 3,936 cases, about ₩29M per case (https://www.straightnews.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=311867 and https://www.ccmessage.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=121353). The two-stage method and the government's own advice to require deposits and reject out-of-scope purchases are described at https://www.viva100.com/article/20250623501489. The same article cites a Hyundai Research Institute estimate that ordinary no-shows cost hospitality ₩4.5 trillion a year, so the scam-defense wedge extends into a much larger deposit-booking market.
first_30_days: Days 1-7: Build a Kakao Channel bot that sends a hosted page with PASS auth, a deposit request via a payment gateway such as Toss Payments, and a scam-pattern checklist. Days 8-20: Offer free pilots to 50 shops via bakery, catering and restaurant owner Kakao open-chat groups and the local Food Service Association branch, with a scam-script sticker for the phone. Days 21-30: Convert the pilots that actually used it, publish a first 'blocked scam' tally, and approach one POS vendor and one card-acquirer with a co-branded offer.

title: Sworn Testator Depositions for the Deepfake Era
one_liner: Estate attorneys refer aging or blended-family clients to a 45-minute sworn Q&A on intent and capacity, taken by a reporter who certifies it and stored in an escrow vault that opens on death. Because a human certified it, it stays credible when video can be faked.
customer: Estate planning and elder law attorneys, whose clients pay $1,200-$3,000 per session (billed through as a cost). Also wealth advisors and family offices serving blended-family, dementia-risk or high-conflict heirs. Trust and estate litigators are a secondary buyer.
problem: The great wealth transfer is driving more will and trust contests over capacity and undue influence. The standard defense is a video of the signing, but anyone can now claim video or audio is synthetic or edited. Attorney file notes look self-serving, and witness memory fades over the 5-15 years between signing and death. Court reporters are the one neutral officer who can administer an oath and certify a verbatim record. Only litigation agencies dispatch reporters, so estate lawyers never think to hire one.
solution: A productized package. A licensed reporter administers the oath. The attorney or an independent examiner runs a structured interview covering assets, family, reasons for unequal splits, and awareness of who might object. An optional treating-physician attestation is added. The client receives a certified transcript, hash-locked and time-stamped video, and the reporter's certificate. Everything goes into an encrypted escrow vault that releases on a death certificate or an attorney trigger. Clients re-sit every 2-3 years. The package maps to ante-mortem probate options in the few states that have them (Ohio and Alaska are examples) and to each state's rules for perpetuating testimony. Admissibility varies by jurisdiction, so attorneys own the legal strategy.
why_now: Deepfakes are making courts wary of unauthenticated audio and video. The federal Advisory Committee on Evidence Rules was still working on a Rule 901(c) deepfake amendment and a new Rule 707 for machine-generated evidence at its October 2026 meeting. Remote depositions and remote-reporting laws such as California's AB 3013 make flexible scheduling normal, and estate sessions can be scheduled unlike litigation work. The wealth transfer is under way now.
revenue_model: $1,200-$3,000 per session, with about 50-60% going to the reporter. Vault fee of about $150 per year. $600 re-sit sessions every 2-3 years, which creates a recurring long tail. No referral fees to attorneys, because ethics rules prohibit fee splitting. Attorneys bill the session as a case cost.
non_obvious_insight: The reporter's certificate and oath are the one part of a transcript AI cannot counterfeit, and its value rises as media authenticity falls. Estate planners sit outside the reporter dispatch network, so nobody has packaged the reporter's authority for them.
first_30_days: Partner with 2 licensed reporters and 1 estate attorney, ideally in a large metro or an ante-mortem-probate state. Write the interview protocol with the attorney and a geriatric psychiatrist consultant. Offer a free pilot to 10 estate and elder-law firms through bar CLE lunches and local ACTEC chapters, targeting one blended-family client each. Aim for 5 paid sessions by day 30.

title: Workforce Pell Approval-as-a-Service
one_liner: A fixed-fee desk that turns a college's short-program idea into an approved Workforce Pell application with employer-demand evidence, outcomes math and state sign-off.
customer: Community colleges, technical colleges, proprietary trade schools, workforce boards and apprenticeship sponsors with 8-15 week programs (EMT, CDL, welding, medical assistant, phlebotomy).
problem: Workforce Pell launched July 1, 2026 but only 5 programs were approved by September 22. Colleges call the process hard and complicated. They lack capacity to prove employer demand, calculate outcome tests and obtain governor and state workforce-board sign-off, while vocational-heavy public two-years grew 11.7% in Spring 2025.
solution: Done-for-you application packages: a local labor-demand memo with job-posting data and employer letters, cost-versus-earnings math, outcomes tracking setup for completion and placement, and state-by-state approval navigation. Design programs to be apprenticeship-linked, because registered apprenticeships with college instruction auto-qualify as in-demand and up to 49% of instruction can be outsourced to employers or unions.
why_now: The program is three months old, states are still building approval procedures, and the first approvals came from Iowa Central (EMT) and Ivy Tech (medical assistant). First movers get enrollment for the 2027 terms.
revenue_model: $12-30k per program application plus $500-1,500 a month for outcomes reporting; optional success fee.
non_obvious_insight: The constraint is not curriculum or students but making programs legible to regulators. Approval capacity is the scarce resource, so whoever standardizes the evidence package becomes the gatekeeper's best friend.
first_30_days: Read the statute and guidance, and pick two states with active approvals. Offer 3 community colleges a fixed price with a partial success guarantee. Publish a free checklist to pull leads from workforce boards.

title: Weather-Indexed Revenue Cover for Outdoor Micro-Businesses
one_liner: Per-day parametric policies that pay out within an hour when rain, heat or smoke hits a vendor's venue, priced from the vendor's own sales history.
customer: Farmers-market vendors, food trucks, festival vendors, ice cream and shaved-ice stands, seasonal farm stands and outdoor fitness operators.
problem: A rain day or heat wave can erase a day's sales and cannot be insured through conventional policies. Margins are thin, and small owners (about 64% of nonemployers in trouble) fall back on personal funds.
solution: Micro-policies bought per market day or season. A fixed payout triggers when measured rainfall, temperature or air quality at the venue exceeds a threshold during the market window. Premium and payout are calibrated to each vendor's baseline sales from POS or bank data, and payment goes out over instant rails. Distribution goes through market associations and POS apps.
why_now: Instant payout rails, POS and bank APIs for baseline sales, cheap gridded weather data, and reinsurer interest in parametric small-business products make this feasible for a small MGA team.
revenue_model: MGA margin on premiums of about $6-15 per vendor-day, plus program fees from market associations.
non_obvious_insight: Basis risk is manageable when triggers are set per venue and per day, and the product is cash within an hour of the rain rather than indemnity after paperwork. Vendors will buy small daily coverage bundled into their booth fee.
first_30_days: Partner with one market association (about 100 vendors) and an MGA or fronting carrier. Structure a season-long pilot under a master policy and price it from vendors' POS history. Track claims and basis risk.

title: Evac Cash: Payout When Ordered to Evacuate
one_liner: A few dollars a month buys a $500-$2,500 wire within hours of an official mandatory evacuation order for your address, covering hurricane, wildfire and burn-scar flood orders.
customer: Renters and lower-to-middle-income homeowners in evacuation zones: Gulf and Florida surge zones, Western wildfire-urban-interface neighborhoods, and LA burn-scar areas. Sold to individuals, through employers of hourly staff (hospitals, hotels, nursing homes, grocers), and through credit unions or municipal 'evac funds'.
problem: Evacuating costs $1,000-$3,000 (gas, hotel, lost shifts, pet boarding) and the money is needed before any claim exists. Cost is a common reason people stay, so the people most exposed are least able to leave. Civil-authority and additional-living-expense cover is slow, receipt-based, often conditional on nearby damage, and many renters lack it.
solution: A parametric contract whose trigger is a legal act. If your geocoded address sits inside a polygon under a mandatory evacuation order, or an NWS flash-flood emergency for a burn scar, the platform pays via FedNow/RTP or a push-to-card within hours. Zone data comes from county emergency-management systems (evacuation-zone platforms and state zone maps). Tiers are priced by zone frequency, with one payout per event per address and a simple app that alerts you and shows your zone. Underwritten via a licensed MGA and fronting carrier, first as employer group policies.
why_now: Address-level, machine-readable evacuation zones are now common. FedNow/RTP make hours-not-weeks payouts cheap. The LA fires of January 2025 made burn-scar exposure vivid, and NOAA CPC/IRI's September 2026 outlooks show a greater than 90% chance of a very strong El Niño this winter, which means heavy rain on fresh burn scars and flash-flood/debris-flow evacuation orders. Parametric reinsurance capacity is plentiful and MGAs want small-ticket distribution.
revenue_model: Premium of roughly $3-$15 per month depending on how often each zone is ordered out (about 1.3-1.5x expected payout), or $1-$3 per employee per month on group plans. The company keeps an MGA commission of 15-25%, plus municipal, nonprofit and employer-funded policies for vulnerable residents. Later it can sell zone-frequency data to emergency managers.
non_obvious_insight: The best parametric trigger is a legal act, not a physical measurement. An evacuation order is binary, public, address-specific and timestamped, so basis risk nearly vanishes. Paying people to leave also changes behavior and saves lives, which makes employers and governments willing co-payers, so the product has two buyers instead of one.
first_30_days: Sign a parametric MGA and fronting carrier. Build the polygon match and instant-payout flow on public evacuation-zone data. Pilot a group policy for about 200 hourly workers at one Gulf hospital or hotel employer and one credit union serving a LA burn-scar community. Offer emergency-management agencies a free 'what zone am I in' tool for distribution. Goal: 500 covered addresses before peak rain season.

title: Professional Health-Care Agents for Solo Agers
one_liner: A subscription 'designated agent' nurse-advocate with health-care proxy authority who is reachable at 2 am, sold to solo agers and to hospitals stuck with unbefriended patients.
customer: Solo agers 70-85 with $300k-$2M in assets and no spouse or children nearby (27% of 65+ live alone). Hospitals and elder-law attorneys are the B2B channels.
problem: Solo agers often lack a health-care proxy. When a crisis hits, hospitals face consent and discharge bottlenecks, and the state may appoint a professional guardian through a slow, expensive court process. Agencies and hospitals can't act as trusted agents because of conflicts of interest.
solution: A nurse- or social-worker-led firm whose individual employees serve as named health-care agents. It handles values interviews and updated directives, a wallet card and QR code hospitals can scan to reach the on-call agent, monthly check-ins, and in-hospital advocacy during admissions and discharge. It coordinates with a separate financial fiduciary. AI documentation tools let one agent serve 60-80 clients. Hospitals can also contract for surrogate support for unbefriended patients.
why_now: Solo-ager demographics and the 80+ cohort are surging (NPR, Jul 2026). SNF and home-care capacity is tightening, so discharge delays cost hospitals more, and family caregivers are stretched by Medicaid retrenchment.
revenue_model: $2,400-4,800 a year subscription plus hourly rates for hospital stays, and $1,500-3,000 per unbefriended-patient episode from hospitals.
non_obvious_insight: Care is available if you can pay, but a trusted person with legal authority who answers at 2 am is the missing product. Because family-based caregiving is the default assumption, almost every caregiver product targets a family that doesn't exist for this cohort.
first_30_days: In one state with friendly proxy law (Washington, Oregon or Colorado), recruit two RN or MSW advocates, sign 10 clients through estate attorneys, and approach two hospital case-management directors with a pilot for unbefriended patients.

title: Organized Play in a Box for New Card Games
one_liner: A managed service that gives new and crowdfunded trading card games tournament software, judge training, local-game-store onboarding and prize logistics.
customer: New TCG publishers with funded campaigns (for example the Cyberpunk TCG, which raised $28.35M on Kickstarter in April 2026), and their distributors.
problem: Pokemon has sold 85B+ cards, and new TCGs live or die by weekly events at local game stores. First-time creators have big print-run budgets but no rules-aware tournament engine, judge program, store network or prize support. Kickstarter success does not equal retention.
solution: Rules-aware tournament software (decklist validation, banlist updates, Swiss pairing), a certified judge program, store onboarding kits (demo decks, promos, shipping), an event calendar and reporting, and results-integrity tooling.
why_now: The TCG boom and $28M crowdfunding raises create a wave of well-funded first-time publishers. Stores will only stock games with events.
revenue_model: $5-25k per month retainer per game plus $10-30 per event and margin on store kits.
non_obvious_insight: Kickstarter funds the print run, but retention is in weekly events, and store owners only back games that have them. The infrastructure is game-agnostic, so it amortizes across many small TCGs.
first_30_days: Pitch 20 creators of funded TCG campaigns above $250k. Run a pilot kit at 20 stores. Assemble an open-source tournament engine and sell the first two retainers.
